# nososim

Simulate hospital outbreaks with changing populations, weighted contacts,
individual transmission rates, and optional interventions.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("CyGei/nososim")
```

## A first outbreak

Create a population of 30 people, then simulate spread from one imported case.
Contacts multiply per-contact transmission rates (`tau`) without normalisation.
The intervention halves transmission hazards from contact day 10.
The simulation uses `simulacr`: numeric `w` values refer to delays 0, 1, 2, etc.,
and contacts on each date produce infections recorded on the following day.

```{r first-outbreak}
library(nososim)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(123)
dates <- as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:20
population <- make_population(
  make_landscape(c(hospital = 30)), dates,
  admissions = function(landscape, date) landscape$available,
  individuals = function(admitted, date) {
    dplyr::mutate(admitted,
      id = paste0("ID_", dplyr::row_number()),
      start = date, end = max(dates), tau = 0.1
    )
  }
)

outbreak <- make_outbreak(
  population, data.frame(id = "ID_1", date_infection = dates[1]),
  w = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3), dates = dates, contacts = get_contacts,
  intervention = function(present, date) {
    matrix(
      if (date >= dates[10]) 0.5 else 0,
      nrow(present), nrow(present),
      dimnames = list(present$id, present$id)
    )
  }
)

outbreak$infections |>
  dplyr::count(date_infection) |>
  ggplot(aes(date_infection, n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#176B65") +
  labs(x = "Infection date", y = "New cases") +
  theme_classic()
```

## Go further

The [getting started guide](https://CyGei.github.io/nososim/articles/nososim.html)
walks through landscapes, patient admissions, staff attendance, and weighted
contacts before simulating an outbreak.
Browse the [function reference](https://CyGei.github.io/nososim/reference/index.html)
for individual function arguments and examples.
